Alright, I need to generate a multi-timeframe trading strategy using the provided market data and requirements. Let me break down the problem step by step.

First, the user provided learning insights which include common indicators like RSI, MA, and MACD, but the requirements specify using ATR, Stochastic, and RSI. So, I'll focus on those three.

The strategy needs to be multi-timeframe, so I'll use both 4-hour and daily timeframes. The entry rules will be based on the 4-hour for timely signals, while the exit rules will use the daily for broader trend confirmation.

For entry rules, I'll use RSI and Stochastic on the 4-hour chart. When RSI is below 30 and Stochastic's %K crosses above %D, it's a bullish signal. Conversely, if RSI is above 70 and %K crosses below %D, it's bearish.

Exit rules will use the daily timeframe. If the daily RSI is below 30, I'll hold the long position, and if it's above 70, I'll hold short. Otherwise, I'll exit.

Risk management is crucial. Using ATR for stop-loss and take-profit levels makes sense because it adapts to volatility. I'll set stop-loss at 2x ATR and take-profit at 3x ATR. Also, implementing a trailing stop-loss will help lock in profits as the price moves favorably.

Position sizing should be based on risk per trade. Using 2% risk per trade and adjusting the position size according to the stop-loss distance ensures consistent risk management.

Volatility consideration is handled by ATR, so the strategy adapts to changing market conditions. The average volume is decent, so liquidity shouldn't be a major issue, but I'll keep an eye on it.

Now, putting it all together, I'll structure the strategy with clear entry and exit rules, risk management, and position sizing. The code will use Pandas for data handling, calculate the indicators, and execute the strategy logic.

I should also make sure the code includes comments for clarity and that all parameters are properly defined. Testing the strategy on historical data will help validate its performance, but since the user didn't provide data, I'll outline the logic clearly.

Finally, I'll format everything into a JSON as specified, ensuring each field is correctly populated with the strategy details.
</think>

```json
{
  "strategy_type": "multi_timeframe",
  "indicators": [
    {
      "name": "ATR",
      "params": {
        "period": 14

    },
    {

        "slow_d_period": 3
      }

      "name": "RSI",
      "params": {
        "period": 14
      }
    }
  ],
  "entry_rules": {
    "long_entry": "RSI (4H) < 30 and Stochastic %K (4H) crosses above Stochastic %D (4H)",
    "short_entry": "RSI (4H) > 70 and Stochastic %K (4H) crosses below Stochastic %D (4H)"
  },
  "exit_rules": {
    "long_exit": "RSI (Daily) > 50 or price reaches take-profit level",
    "short_exit": "RSI (Daily) < 50 or price reaches take-profit level"
  },
  "risk_management": {
    "stop_loss_trailing": {
      "type": "atr_trailing",

        "risk_per_trade": 0.02,
        "stop_loss_pips": 20
      }
    }
  },
  "code": "from pandas import DataFrame\nimport numpy as np\nfrom stock_indicators import ATR, Stochastic, RSI\n\n# Define strategy parameters\nclass Strategy:\n    def __init__(self, data, timeframe='4H'):\n        self.data = data\n        self.timeframe = timeframe\n        self.atr = ATR(data, period=14)\n        self.stoch = Stochastic(data, fast_k_period=14, slow_k_period=3, slow_d_period=3)\n        self.rsi = RSI(data, period=14)\n\n    def get_signals(self):\n        signals = DataFrame(index=self.data.index)\n        signals['long_entry'] = False\n        signals['short_entry'] = False\n        signals['long_exit'] = False\n        signals['short_exit'] = False\n\n        # Calculate indicators\n        signals['rsi'] = self.rsi.rsi()\n        signals['stoch_k'] = self.stoch.k()\n        signals['stoch_d'] = self.stoch.d()\n        signals['atr'] = self.atr.atr()\n\n        # Generate entry signals\n        signals.loc[(signals['rsi'] < 30) & (signals['stoch_k'] > signals['stoch_d']), 'long_entry'] = True\n        signals.loc[(signals['rsi'] > 70) & (signals['stoch_k'] < signals['stoch_d']), 'short_entry'] = True\n\n        # Generate exit signals\n        signals.loc[(signals['rsi'] > 50), 'long_exit'] = True\n        signals.loc[(signals['rsi'] < 50), 'short_exit'] = True\n\n        return signals\n\n# Risk management functions\ndef calculate_position_size(account_size, risk_per_trade, stop_loss_pips, atr):\n    position_size = (account_size * risk_per_trade) / stop_loss_pips\n    return position_size\n\n# Strategy execution\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    from backtrader import Cerebro, Position\n    cerebro = Cerebro()\n    cerebro.addstrategy(Strategy)\n    cerebro.run()\n    cerebro.plot()"
}
```
